title: Executive Secretaries and Executive Administrative Assistants

tasks.short: Manage executive calendars, agree meeting times and resolve changes.

steps.what: Read incoming requests in the {EMAIL} and record meeting requirements.

loop.input: Meeting request and relevant thread.
loop.output: Draft purpose, participants, duration, deadline and constraints, with source passages.
loop.check: Validate dates and participant identities; flag missing or contradictory fields.
loop.stop: One extraction per request; incomplete or ambiguous requests enter the assistant's queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requesters express timing and constraints in varied free text; structured submissions bypass the loop.

steps.what: Judge urgency, purpose and executive priorities.
Compare availability and identify workable slots in the {CALENDAR}.
Agree a slot and negotiate clashes through the {EMAIL}.
Create invitations, meeting links and reminders in the {CALENDAR}.
Check responses, cancellations and new conflicts in the {CALENDAR}.
Resolve disruptions and agree changes to executive commitments.

tasks.design: Configure availability, buffers, booking options and reminders in the {CALENDAR}, with a request register in the {WORKFLOW}. A bounded extractor turns unstructured {EMAIL} requests into drafts; the assistant judges priority and agrees sensitive changes. Invitations use confirmed details and delegated scheduling authority.
tasks.previous_blocker: Availability was already digital, but preferences and exceptions lived in conversations and disconnected request threads.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking configuration handles routine coordination; small integrations and bounded extraction reduce request entry work.
tasks.still_hard: Political priorities, unavailable external diaries and last-minute changes still require negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when access to the executive matters more than apparent calendar availability.

ambition.what: Weekly executive time-allocation review across strategic work, preparation and meetings.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more of the week protecting preparation time and resolving competing commitments. With explicit delegation, they can offer alternatives or decline requests outside agreed meeting criteria.

reach.task: Align milestone meetings with project dependencies.
reach.learn: Dependency mapping, decision deadlines and meeting criticality.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can create an invitation and agenda from a mail thread.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation found scheduling took longer; gains need local verification.
Configured availability rules and reminders can remove routine diary comparison and follow-up.

assumptions: This baseline gives more time to calendar screens and negotiation than the supplied means prior.
Routine invitations can use delegated authority after participants agree the details.
Build ranges are working effort; access and consultation waiting can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which diaries expose availability, and which require manual coordination?
Which meetings may the assistant accept, decline or move without executive approval?
Which calendar permissions and request-processing capabilities are available?
Do national rules require employee consultation for the proposed configuration?
research_questions: Which request types benefit from booking links, and which create more coordination work?
Does a pilot reduce total scheduling time without increasing corrections or executive interruptions?
new_work: Review ambiguous request extractions.
Maintain buffers, meeting categories and delegated scheduling limits.
Check failed invitations and permission changes.
Sample completed bookings for incorrect participants, time zones or confidentiality.
tasks.statement: Manage and maintain executives' schedules.

tasks.short: Prepare financial documents, reports and executive correspondence from approved records.

steps.what: Clarify purpose, audience, document type and deadline with the requester.
Retrieve approved financial figures and transaction records from the {ERP}.
Reconcile totals, calculate tables and investigate differences in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Prepare invoice drafts from billable records in the {ERP}.
Populate report, statement and correspondence templates in the {DOCS}.
Write tailored explanations, memos and letters in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Document brief, populated template and approved source records.
loop.output: Tailored narrative with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Match names and figures to records; reject unsupported claims; assistant checks tone and meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one correction pass; unresolved claims remain flagged for the approver.
loop.why_not_simpler: Audience-specific explanations and correspondence exceed fixed wording; standard passages remain deterministic.

steps.what: Approve financial statements, invoice details and accounting exceptions.
Approve executive correspondence, interpretations and commitments.
Send approved documents to authorised recipients through the {EMAIL}.
File final versions and approval records in the {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Use configured invoice generation in the {ERP} and deterministic jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} to reconcile approved figures and populate templates in the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop handles tailored narrative, while the {WORKFLOW} routes financial and executive approvals separately. Approved versions go through the {EMAIL} to validated recipients and are archived with their approval records.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents mixed reusable formatting with inconsistent source records, manual reconciliation and bespoke wording.
tasks.enabler_now: Template generation and arithmetic need ordinary code; faster implementation makes small source mappings and validation rules economical.
tasks.still_hard: Source discrepancies, accounting interpretation and statements that commit the organisation still need accountable review.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when technically correct figures or wording would give the recipient a misleading impression.

ambition.what: Weekly departmental spending-variance review using reconciled figures.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time resolving missing evidence and preparing decision-ready explanations. They can return incomplete briefs and request corrections to source data; financial sign-off remains with finance.

reach.task: Explain departmental spending variances and their operational causes.
reach.learn: Reconciliation, metric definitions and evidence-based variance analysis.

evidence.claim: Structured records can populate document templates, and deterministic checks can reconcile totals.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported drafting time savings but also hallucinations and no evidence of higher productivity.
The proposed document pipeline and its remaining-time estimates have no directly matching case in the digest.

assumptions: Shares describe a mixed document portfolio; individual requests follow only the relevant branches.
The assistant prepares financial material from approved records rather than deciding accounting treatment.
The assistant has access to authorised financial extracts.
Only approved versions and recipient lists permit automatic dispatch.
Build ranges cover a bounded initial template set and working effort, including access and consultation preparation.
unknowns: Which document types dominate volume and preparation time?
Which records are authoritative, and how often do totals disagree?
Which templates and calculations already exist in the {ERP} or {DOCS}?
Who must approve each financial document and external commitment?
What GDPR retention, access and national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Which templates can use structured fields and approved wording without a model?
Which reconciliation failures require accounting judgement rather than data correction?
Does narrative drafting reduce total preparation and approval time?
new_work: Maintain templates, field mappings and calculation definitions.
Resolve failed reconciliations and missing source records.
Review narrative claims, tone and source references.
Maintain approver routes, recipient controls and retention rules.
tasks.statement: Prepare invoices, reports, memos, letters, financial statements, and other documents, using word processing, spreadsheet, database, or presentation software.

tasks.short: Assess incoming material, decide its significance and arrange appropriate distribution.

steps.what: Collect incoming memos, submissions and reports.
Read documents and identify requests, deadlines and relevant background.

loop.input: Accessible incoming material and its document metadata.
loop.output: A brief containing requests, deadlines, named parties and source passages.
loop.check: Require a source passage for each finding; flag missing dates and conflicting statements.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unreadable or unsupported items return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests and deadlines appear in varied prose and document layouts.

steps.what: Judge significance, sensitivity and the need for executive attention.
Select recipients and specify the action expected from each.
Forward material and record its distribution.

tasks.design: Configure the {EMAIL} review queue and use a bounded extraction step to create source-linked briefs in the {DOCS}. The assistant judges significance, approves recipients in the {WORKFLOW}, and releases permission-checked internal distribution through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Routing depends on executive context, confidentiality and informal relationships. Earlier rules could sort senders but could not reliably interpret varied documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing queue rules handle collection and delivery. Bounded extraction can prepare traceable briefs, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and permissions.
tasks.still_hard: Political significance, implied urgency and permission boundaries remain difficult. A correct summary can still miss why an issue matters.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant understands competing priorities, notices sensitive implications and knows when private escalation is better than wider circulation.

ambition.what: A daily executive attention brief with explicit escalation decisions.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from reading every page and forwarding attachments toward assessing competing issues and checking follow-through. Formal decision rights do not change; escalation authority remains delegated by the executive.

reach.task: Prepare issue briefs that compare implications across departments.
reach.learn: Problem framing, evidence quality and how to distinguish a signal from background detail.

evidence.claim: Queue rules and permission-aware distribution can automate collection and delivery; contextual significance remains human judgement.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation observed hallucinations and found no evidence of higher productivity; local validation is necessary.
Step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates rather than measured outcomes.

assumptions: The representative workflow distributes material internally; external disclosure requires separate authority.
Time shares describe a typical task instance, not a measured customer baseline.
Build ranges cover a limited pilot using existing systems and exclude waiting for procurement or consultation decisions.
GDPR access limits, purpose limitation and retention apply to the brief as well as the original material.
unknowns: Which executive priorities and escalation thresholds the assistant may apply independently.
Whether document permissions can be checked before distribution.
The volume of scanned files, restricted attachments and exceptional recipient lists.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
research_questions: Does source-linked extraction reduce reading time without missing significant issues?
Can existing queue and permission features support the pilot without custom integration?
new_work: Check unsupported findings and conflicting deadlines.
Maintain distribution groups, access rules and escalation criteria.
Sample briefs for missed context and inappropriate recipient suggestions.
Monitor connector failures and document retention.
tasks.statement: Read and analyze incoming memos, submissions, and reports to determine their significance and plan their distribution.

tasks.short: Receive, sort and distribute electronic and physical correspondence.

steps.what: Collect incoming email and electronic fax attachments.
Open permitted physical mail and scan items needing electronic distribution.
Read correspondence and identify its recipient, urgency and confidentiality.

loop.input: Correspondence, extracted document text and a permission-scoped routing directory.
loop.output: Recipient recommendation, handling category, supporting text spans and exception flags.
loop.check: Use exact recipient rules first; validate destinations and permissions, and flag unreadable or conflicting text.
loop.stop: At most one model classification per unmatched item; ambiguous, restricted or unreadable items go to review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Address and sender rules cover known items; free-text requests often lack a clear department or owner.

steps.what: Resolve unclear ownership and decide how to handle sensitive or urgent items.
Forward electronic items and file copies in the appropriate record.
Deliver physical originals or place them in designated collection points.

tasks.design: Configure intake from {EMAIL} and scanning into {DOCS}, with a routing directory and receipt log in {WORKFLOW}. Exact rules route permitted routine items; a bounded classifier proposes destinations for unmatched text, with human approval before any model-derived destination is used. Deliver physical originals in batches where deadlines and handling rules permit.
tasks.previous_blocker: The mailbox and physical tray lacked a shared ownership map. Rules were brittle when letters named issues rather than recipients.
tasks.enabler_now: Intake rules, text extraction and receipt logs are established technology. A small model step can suggest destinations for unmatched text without controlling distribution.
tasks.still_hard: Sealed personal mail, poor scans, legal deadlines and politically sensitive correspondence need careful handling. Physical originals still move by hand.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant recognises organisational significance and knows when formal ownership differs from the person who must be alerted.

ambition.what: A tracked receipt-to-owner service for time-critical executive correspondence.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time opening electronic queues and repeatedly forwarding items. They can track unacknowledged time-critical items and escalate through an agreed path; authority over their substance stays with the recipient.

reach.task: Maintain correspondence classification and retention records.
reach.learn: Record identifiers, restricted access, original-document handling and retention schedules.

reach.task: Define receipt and escalation arrangements for time-critical correspondence.
reach.learn: Handoff measurement, service ownership and exception analysis.

evidence.claim: Mailbox rules and routing directories can automate known electronic correspondence patterns without a model.
Bounded text classification can propose destinations, but the digest supplies no measured case for this executive-mail workflow.

assumptions: Electronic correspondence dominates item volume; physical mail consumes a larger share of handling time per item.
The prior classification as mainly human work understates rule-based electronic routing, but correctly signals physical and confidential exceptions.
Only exact, approved rules route without review; every model-derived destination needs a recorded human routing decision.
Ordinary routing decisions are supplied by approved rules; the human decision step handles unmatched and sensitive items.
Build ranges include one shared intake, GDPR and access review, plus applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Physical, email and fax volumes and the actual time spent on each.
Rules for opening personal, confidential and legally significant mail.
Whether scanning, mailbox and document-store access can be connected.
Who owns the routing directory and acknowledges time-critical items.
Retention requirements and applicable consultation arrangements.
research_questions: How much volume can exact recipient and sender rules cover?
Which correspondence categories must always remain in restricted review?
Can a pilot reduce handling time without increasing misroutes, missed deadlines or duplicate records?
new_work: Review unmatched, sensitive and unreadable items.
Maintain routing ownership and access restrictions.
Resolve failed deliveries, duplicates and missing acknowledgements.
Check that scanned copies and physical originals remain correctly linked.
tasks.statement: Open, sort, and distribute incoming correspondence, including faxes and email.

tasks.short: Classify, file, retrieve and share corporate documents with appropriate access.

steps.what: Receive documents and check whether a final version has already been filed.
Identify document type, business context and required filing metadata.

loop.input: Unclassified document, approved taxonomy and permitted metadata values.
loop.output: Proposed document type and metadata with supporting passages.
loop.check: Validate allowed values and required fields; use structured source labels first and route conflicts to review.
loop.stop: One classification pass per document; missing evidence or uncertain classification goes to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules handle known templates, but irregular documents lack reliable metadata.

steps.what: File the document with its version, access group and retention category.
Clarify which document the requester needs and their intended use.
Search the document store and confirm the correct version.
Check the requester's access and send the document or a controlled link.

tasks.design: Configure intake, version control, metadata, retention categories and permission-aware search in {DOCS}, using {WORKFLOW} for intake from {EMAIL}. Deterministic rules handle known document types; a bounded classifier proposes metadata for irregular documents, while reviewed filing and release actions preserve access boundaries.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents arrive through inconsistent channels, naming conventions vary, and historical access groups are poorly maintained.
tasks.enabler_now: Document stores already support metadata, versioning and access-controlled search. AI-assisted coding makes intake connections cheaper, and bounded classification can reduce manual tagging.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy permissions, ambiguous final versions, legal holds and missing context need human decisions. Better retrieval depends heavily on cleaning the underlying records.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant understands why a record matters and recognises when an apparently valid request deserves discretion.

ambition.what: Permission-controlled self-service retrieval for newly appointed committee members.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time searching folders and more time resolving access and record-quality exceptions. They can correct metadata within agreed categories; disclosure rights and retention policy remain unchanged.

reach.task: Improve classification and retrieval of shared records.
reach.learn: Metadata design, version control, retention categories and permission testing.

evidence.claim: Metadata, version control, retention labels and permission-aware search are established document-management capabilities.
Bounded classification can propose metadata, but source permissions and retention decisions require separate controls.

assumptions: Most records are digital; large-scale paper scanning is outside the build estimate.
The document store remains the authoritative record and enforces access at retrieval.
Classification never grants access, deletes records or overrides a legal hold.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
GDPR applies to personal records; retention and employee consultation requirements also depend on national rules.
Legacy migration is a separate work package if records or permissions need extensive repair.
unknowns: How many stores contain authoritative records, and how much paper remains?
Are access groups, retention categories and legal holds defined and current?
Which documents require owner approval before filing or disclosure?
What migration volume, access review and employee consultation will be necessary?
research_questions: Can configured metadata search meet retrieval needs before semantic search is considered?
Which document categories produce ambiguous classifications?
Can permission tests demonstrate that search results and links respect existing access?
new_work: Review uncertain metadata and sensitive document releases.
Maintain taxonomy, access groups and retention mappings.
Resolve duplicate versions and missing ownership.
Test search permissions and audit filing exceptions.
tasks.statement: File and retrieve corporate documents, records, and reports.

tasks.short: Welcome visitors, confirm their purpose and control access to executives.

steps.what: Welcome the visitor and ask whom they are visiting.
Check the appointment and relevant visitor instructions.
Contact the host to confirm readiness or request access for an unexpected visitor.
Confirm, defer or refuse the visit within the visitor policy.
Register the approved visitor and print a badge in visitor-management software.
Explain access conditions and escort or hand over the visitor.

tasks.design: Configure visitor-management software in {OTHER} to read only approved visitor details from {CALENDAR} and notify the host through {CHAT}. Record the host's decision before badge release, with prefilled registration and a manual fallback. The assistant welcomes visitors, checks required details and manages the handover; no model or automated visitor scoring is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appointment details, host contact and visitor registration were disconnected. Much of the supporting work was already configurable.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar links, host notifications and prefilled registration can remove repeat entry. Small connectors can be built faster when existing configuration is insufficient.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected arrivals, identity discrepancies, unavailable hosts and tense refusals remain interpersonal and security-sensitive.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant offers a welcome, notices situational concerns and explains a delay or refusal respectfully.

ambition.what: Visitors who need step-free routes or a quieter arrival, through an optional arrival-assistance request.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into appointment searches and chasing hosts. The assistant can coordinate agreed arrival assistance; the host's invitation never overrides the visitor policy, and security decision rights do not expand.

reach.task: Coordinate accessible visitor routes and arrival assistance.
reach.learn: Accessible routes, practical assistance options and escalation to building staff.

evidence.claim: Appointment matching, host notifications and prefilled visitor registration can use deterministic configuration.
The digest supplies no documented visitor-access case or measured saving for this workflow.

assumptions: A staffed office uses visitor-management software; a paper register would change the current means and integration scope.
Shares represent active handling time across the assistant and host, excluding unattended waiting.
Host confirmation may be recorded before arrival; a visitor without valid authorisation remains with the assistant.
The low prior for replacing the whole task is appropriate, while appointment lookup and host notification can still change.
Arrival assistance records only requested practical arrangements, without collecting a diagnosis.
Build ranges include calendar access, GDPR review, reception rollout and applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Whether visitor-management software exists and supports calendar and host-notification connections.
Who may approve entry and which checks the assistant must perform.
Visitor volumes, unexpected-arrival frequency and host response times.
Available accessible routes and staffing for arrival assistance.
Visitor-data retention and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Can visitor details be shared without exposing unrelated calendar information?
Does the configured flow reduce active handling without delaying walk-ins?
Can optional arrival assistance be arranged using minimal, short-lived information?
new_work: Maintain host contacts, visitor instructions and access permissions.
Resolve missing approvals, stale appointments and badge failures.
Delete visitor data according to the retention schedule.
Coordinate requested arrival assistance and maintain the manual fallback.
tasks.statement: Greet visitors and determine whether they should be given access to specific individuals.

tasks.short: Prepare, check and send responses to routine correspondence.

steps.what: Read the inquiry and identify the requested answer.

loop.input: Incoming correspondence and an approved list of routine inquiry types.
loop.output: Inquiry brief with requested facts, inquiry type and exception flags.
loop.check: Require supporting text spans; validate the type against the list and flag unclear or sensitive requests.
loop.stop: One classification pass per message; unresolved requests enter the assistant's exception queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Sender and subject rules handle known patterns, but differently worded requests need limited text interpretation.

steps.what: Find current facts, policies and approved wording.
Draft a reply using the facts and an appropriate template.

loop.input: Inquiry brief, permission-filtered response facts and approved response template.
loop.output: Response draft with internal source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Validate inserted fields; require sources for factual statements and reject unsupported commitments.
loop.stop: Use template-only generation where possible; otherwise allow one model draft with no automatic retries.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard answers; mixed questions sometimes require short, source-grounded prose.

steps.what: Check accuracy, disclosure and tone; approve or escalate the reply.
Send the approved reply and retain the correspondence.

tasks.design: Map routine inquiry types to approved facts and templates in {DOCS}, with bounded classification and drafting only where fixed rules cannot handle the wording. Present the draft and its sources beside the inquiry in {EMAIL}; send and file only the version the assistant approves. Begin with one authorised mailbox and expand the source library by inquiry type.
tasks.previous_blocker: Approved wording and current facts were difficult to find. Fixed templates did not handle several questions in one message.
tasks.enabler_now: A small source index and template generator are straightforward to build. Bounded models can interpret varied wording and draft from supplied facts, subject to review.
tasks.still_hard: Outdated guidance, hidden commitments and requests outside delegated authority still require clarification or escalation.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant understands the relationship, recognises implied commitments and chooses a suitable level of disclosure.

ambition.what: A weekly briefing on recurring unanswered inquiries, with proposed guidance changes.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into finding wording and composing routine replies. The assistant can recommend guidance changes from recurring inquiries; policy approval remains with the relevant owner.

reach.task: Analyse recurring inquiries and identify missing or conflicting guidance.
reach.learn: Basic inquiry coding, trend interpretation and process recommendation writing.

evidence.claim: The UK Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported mean drafting time savings of 1.3 hours per studied task; this is not an estimate for routine replies.
That evaluation observed hallucinations and found no evidence of higher productivity, supporting continued review rather than assumed gains.
Approved templates and permission-filtered fact lookup can handle fixed answers without a language model.

assumptions: Most inquiries are routine, but the prior probability of near-total automation overstates the removal of disclosure and commitment checks.
Response facts can be indexed by inquiry type; missing facts trigger escalation rather than open-ended searching.
Approval attaches to the exact recipient, attachments and response version; edits invalidate approval.
Build ranges are estimates for a limited inquiry library and one mailbox, including access review, GDPR checks, AI literacy and applicable employee consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which inquiry types are genuinely routine and within the assistant's authority.
Whether approved guidance has named owners and reliable version dates.
Mailbox permissions, retention requirements and allowed model-processing arrangements.
Actual inquiry mix, current drafting effort and review effort.
research_questions: What share of replies can use fixed templates without model drafting?
Can every factual sentence be checked against an approved source?
Does a trial reduce total preparation and review time while preserving accuracy and appropriate disclosure?
new_work: Review response drafts and resolve unsupported facts.
Maintain templates, source mappings and guidance versions.
Investigate misclassification and prevent duplicate sends.
Prepare the weekly briefing on gaps in approved guidance.
tasks.statement: Prepare responses to correspondence containing routine inquiries.

tasks.short: Arrange executive travel, confirm bookings and manage disruptions.

steps.what: Read travel requirements and preferences from the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Travel request and relevant correspondence.
loop.output: Draft destinations, dates, arrival constraints and preferences with source passages.
loop.check: Validate dates and locations; distinguish explicit requirements from preferences; flag missing fields.
loop.stop: One extraction; unresolved fields go to the assistant before option selection.
loop.why_not_simpler: Unstructured requests mix appointments, preferences and travel constraints; structured forms bypass the loop.

steps.what: Search transport and accommodation in the {OTHER} travel booking system.
Compare timing, total cost and cancellation terms in a {SPREADSHEET}.
Choose an itinerary and approve its cost and policy exceptions.
Book the approved option in the {OTHER} travel booking system.
Assemble tickets, accommodation details and local transfers in the {DOCS}.
Send the itinerary and update travel blocks in the {CALENDAR}.
Resolve disruptions and negotiate replacement arrangements by phone.

tasks.design: Use a travel request form in the {WORKFLOW} and configured searches in the {OTHER} travel booking system, with deterministic comparisons of cost, timing and policy. A bounded loop reads requests arriving through the {EMAIL}; approved bookings generate an itinerary in the {DOCS} and travel blocks in the {CALENDAR}. Revalidate live price and terms at the booking gate, and return disruption costs through the approval route.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preferences, quotes, approvals and confirmations were scattered; booking access and supplier interfaces varied.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured travel searches, structured approvals and inexpensive comparison and itinerary generators can connect the routine work.
tasks.still_hard: Changing availability, cancellation conditions, accessibility needs and disruptions require judgement and supplier negotiation.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a workable journey under pressure and knowing which inconvenience the executive will accept.

ambition.what: A pre-trip readiness check covering connection buffers, local transfers and cancellation deadlines.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time assembling options and more time checking journey resilience. With delegation, they can choose replacements within an approved disruption budget.

reach.task: Review travel supplier performance and recurring service failures.
reach.learn: Fare conditions, supplier service measures and total trip cost.

evidence.claim: Structured travel policies support deterministic filtering, comparison and approval routing.
Confirmed booking records can populate itinerary templates and calendar entries without a model.

assumptions: The baseline includes a travel booking system and occasional manual comparison of mixed quotes.
The target requires supported search and booking configuration; unsupported suppliers remain manual.
Travel approval and final transaction checks are separate actions.
Build ranges cover working effort; supplier access and consultation waiting can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which booking systems and supplier interfaces are available?
Who approves cost, policy exceptions and disruption spending?
Can booking confirmations be retrieved as structured records?
Which traveller data may be stored, shared and retained under GDPR?
What access approvals or national consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: How much travel uses supported suppliers rather than bespoke arrangements?
Can quoted totals and cancellation terms be validated again immediately before purchase?
Which itinerary checks catch the most consequential travel problems?
new_work: Maintain policy limits and traveller preferences.
Check live prices, passenger identity and cancellation terms before booking.
Handle unsupported suppliers and failed confirmation imports.
Maintain itinerary templates and delete unnecessary traveller data.
tasks.statement: Make travel arrangements for executives.

tasks.short: Research topics, reconcile supporting data and prepare executive or board papers.

steps.what: Clarify the decision, scope, audience and deadline with the executive.
Find relevant internal reports and request missing departmental information.
Search public research databases in {OTHER} and record relevant sources.

loop.input: Research brief and documents returned by approved database searches.
loop.output: Evidence table with quotations, dates, source locations and stated limitations.
loop.check: Require a retrieved passage for every claim; the assistant checks relevance and source credibility.
loop.stop: At most five searches and twenty documents per brief; stop at the cap and return coverage gaps.
loop.why_not_simpler: Search rules retrieve documents, but relevant claims occur in varied prose.

steps.what: Reconcile figures, calculate comparisons and prepare supporting tables.
Write the paper, evidence summary, options and unresolved questions.

loop.input: Research brief, reviewed evidence table, validated figures and paper template.
loop.output: Draft paper with cited claims, options, uncertainties and a decision request.
loop.check: Resolve citations to supplied evidence, compare every figure with validated data, and flag unsupported conclusions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per paper; unresolved claims remain flagged for the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot synthesize mixed evidence or express trade-offs in useful prose.

steps.what: Review conclusions and approve the paper for its intended audience.
File the approved paper and circulate access links to authorised recipients.

tasks.design: A controlled job on {DATA_PLATFORM} gathers permitted reports from {DOCS} and {BI}, retrieves approved external sources through {OTHER}, and calculates tables with deterministic rules. Bounded extraction and drafting loops produce a cited paper in {DOCS}; executive approval releases it through {WORKFLOW} to a fixed distribution list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source permissions, inconsistent definitions and bespoke requests made each paper a separate assembly exercise.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors, reusable calculations and document templates already exist. Bounded models can extract and draft prose, while AI-assisted coding makes the surrounding assembly cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Source credibility, incompatible figures and politically consequential conclusions remain difficult. The high automation prior does not remove executive review or evidence checking.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant understands the decision behind the request and recognises which missing fact could change it.

ambition.what: A monthly review of evidence gaps behind pending executive decisions.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time testing evidence and framing options. They gain authority to return incomplete briefs and request source clarification; executives retain recommendations and decisions.

reach.task: Compare operational options for an executive decision.
reach.learn: Source evaluation, metric definitions, scenario analysis and explicit uncertainty.

evidence.claim: The UK departmental evaluation observed time savings in drafting, but hallucinations and no evidence of higher productivity.
The digest contains no documented case establishing reliable autonomous executive research.
Permission-aware retrieval, reproducible calculations and source-linked drafting can be combined without an autonomous agent.

assumptions: Research supports management decisions and does not require specialist legal or investment advice.
Recurring internal sources can be identified; novel research still needs manual source selection.
Circulation uses the executive-approved paper and a pre-authorised recipient list.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
GDPR applies to personal information in source material; model access must preserve source permissions.
unknowns: Which research databases and internal reports are licensed and accessible?
Who validates financial and operational metric definitions?
How often do papers concern highly restricted or personal information?
What approval, retention and distribution rules apply to board papers?
research_questions: Can reviewers trace material claims to evidence faster than they can check today's papers?
Which recurring paper types have sufficiently stable inputs and calculations?
How much review time remains after accounting for unsupported claims and contradictory sources?
new_work: Review evidence relevance, citations and conflicting definitions.
Maintain source connectors, metric mappings and paper templates.
Resolve access failures and research coverage gaps.
Sample approved papers for unsupported claims and stale evidence.
tasks.statement: Conduct research, compile data, and prepare papers for consideration and presentation by executives, committees, and boards of directors.

tasks.short: Prepare accurate meeting minutes, obtain approval and distribute the approved record.

steps.what: Collect the agenda, attendance list and supporting papers.
Take notes during the meeting and capture decisions and actions.
Compile notes into structured minutes using the meeting template.

loop.input: Permitted transcript or meeting notes, agenda, attendance and minutes template.
loop.output: Draft minutes and actions with references to supporting source passages.
loop.check: Verify decisions, owners, dates, attendance and dissent; flag unsupported or ambiguous statements.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unclear decisions go to the assistant and chair.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free speech and notes require semantic interpretation; a template alone cannot identify decisions reliably.

steps.what: Resolve unclear decisions, action owners and disputed wording with participants.
Approve the minutes and authorised distribution list.
File approved minutes, distribute them and enter agreed actions.

tasks.design: Configure permitted meeting capture and source collection, storing restricted material in {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop produces referenced minutes and action candidates; the assistant resolves uncertainty and the chair approves the record and recipients. A flow in {WORKFLOW} files the approved version, distributes it through {EMAIL} and creates agreed actions in {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual notes need substantial rewriting, and decisions are often implicit. Earlier transcription and summaries still required careful correction.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing meeting tools can capture notes, while bounded drafting can organise them into a controlled template. Approval and distribution already fit standard workflow features.
tasks.still_hard: Speaker attribution, dissent, confidential discussion and ambiguous decisions remain difficult. Formal meeting rules may require approval beyond the chair.
tasks.human_edge: Know what the meeting actually agreed, preserve meaningful disagreement and challenge wording that overstates a decision.

ambition.what: A weekly cross-meeting decision and dependency brief for the executive.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time transcribing and formatting, and more time confirming decisions and exposing dependencies. Authority to approve minutes remains with the meeting's designated approver.

reach.task: Identify dependencies across agreed meeting actions.
reach.learn: Link actions to decisions and milestones without treating a proposed action as an approved commitment.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Teams Facilitator provides live meeting notes.
iBabs Debrief provides board-meeting transcripts, summaries and minutes.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported meeting-summary time savings and observed hallucinations.

Time shares cover active minutes-production effort, including clarification and approval; they exclude passive meeting attendance.
Configured capture is used only after the organisation establishes the lawful basis, participant information, access and retention.
Where recording is unsuitable, the drafting loop uses typed notes and capture savings will be smaller.
GDPR applies to transcripts and minutes. Assess whether transcription requires a DPIA and provide relevant EU AI Act literacy.
Works-council or employee consultation depends on national rules. Consent-and-access ranges estimate effort; elapsed consultation may be longer.
The chair is the assumed approver; formal governance rules may require a different approval route.
unknowns: Which meetings may be recorded or transcribed.
Whether existing meeting tools provide suitable capture and restricted storage.
Who formally approves each type of minutes.
Which recipients, retention periods and national consultation requirements apply.
How often decisions or speaker identities are unclear.

How much review time remains for multilingual meetings and contested decisions?
Can every proposed action be traced to an explicit agreement?
Does the pilot reduce total capture, correction and approval effort?
new_work: Check capture quality and handle missing sections.
Review decisions, attribution, dissent and action ownership.
Maintain templates, recipient lists and approval routes.
Apply retention rules to recordings, transcripts and approved records.
Track correction rates and disable capture where it adds more work than it saves.
tasks.statement: Compile, transcribe, and distribute minutes of meetings.

tasks.short: Attend meetings, draft accurate minutes and arrange their approval, circulation and filing.

steps.what: Review the agenda, meeting papers and previous minutes.
Attend the meeting and capture notes using conferencing software.
Turn meeting notes into minutes containing decisions, actions and owners.

loop.input: An authorised meeting transcript or human notes, agenda and meeting papers.
loop.output: Draft minutes with source-linked decisions, actions, owners and explicitly stated deadlines.
loop.check: Trace decisions to source passages; flag disputed wording, uncertain speakers and missing owners without inventing them.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision after review; unresolved decisions return to the assistant and chair.
loop.why_not_simpler: Discussion is unstructured, and a template cannot distinguish proposals from agreed decisions.

steps.what: Resolve disputed wording and approve the official minutes.
Circulate approved minutes to the authorised attendee list.
File the approved version with the meeting records.

tasks.design: Generate an agenda-based template from the {DOCS} and configure authorised transcription in the conferencing software represented by {OTHER}. A bounded drafting step prepares source-linked minutes for assistant review and chair approval; the {WORKFLOW} then controls circulation through the {EMAIL} and filing in the {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capturing discussion and distinguishing decisions from debate required sustained attention. Earlier transcription alone left substantial drafting and checking work.
tasks.enabler_now: Meeting transcription and draft-note features already exist. Bounded drafting can follow a fixed minutes structure, with ordinary approval and retention controls around it.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive meetings may prohibit recording or require full human attendance. Overlapping speech, implied agreement and formal approval requirements still demand judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices unresolved disagreement, asks for a clear decision and preserves an accurate record without flattening sensitive discussion.

ambition.what: A searchable decision history for recurring leadership meetings.

tasks.altitude: For routine recordable meetings, the assistant spends less time transcribing and more time confirming decisions and following up unclear actions. The chair retains approval authority; the assistant gains no new formal decision rights.

reach.task: Track meeting actions through to evidenced completion.
reach.learn: Action ownership, dependency tracking and clear completion criteria.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Teams Facilitator provides live meeting notes, supporting configured capture rather than bespoke transcription development.
iBabs Debrief provides transcripts, summaries and board-meeting minutes; this establishes capability, not local accuracy or savings.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported meeting-summary time savings and observed hallucinations.
In the Netherlands, works-council consent requirements can apply to employee-data and monitoring arrangements introduced with transcription.
AI literacy requirements apply; ordinary minutes drafting is not itself an Annex III employment use.
The proposed remaining effort and build ranges are estimates for routine, authorised, recordable meetings.

assumptions: The reduced capture time assumes the assistant need not attend every minute solely to take notes.
Meetings requiring full attendance or prohibiting recording retain more manual work.
The chair can approve minutes under the meeting's governance rules; some bodies require wider approval.
Recording requires an appropriate GDPR basis, participant information, controlled access and defined retention; a chair's approval alone is insufficient.
Consent and access ranges cover working effort, including consultation preparation; elapsed consultation time may be longer.
unknowns: Which meetings permit recording and which require full assistant attendance.
Applicable national consultation rules and existing recording agreements.
Whether a DPIA is required for the proposed processing.
Required languages, audio quality, approval rules and retention periods.
Whether the attendee list includes external participants requiring separate distribution controls.
research_questions: How often do draft minutes confuse a proposal with an agreed decision?
Does capture review plus editing save time for each meeting type?
Can existing document metadata support a searchable decision history without another repository?
new_work: Check uncertain speakers, decisions, owners and deadlines against source material.
Resolve corrections with the chair before publication.
Maintain recording permissions, participant information and deletion schedules.
Test minute quality across languages, accents and meeting formats.
Maintain the approved decision index and remove superseded drafts.
tasks.statement: Attend meetings to record minutes.

tasks.short: Represent executives or governing groups in meetings and report agreed outcomes.

steps.what: Clarify the meeting purpose, authorised position and limits on commitments.
Review background correspondence and prepare a meeting brief.

loop.input: Authorised background documents, agenda and representation mandate.
loop.output: Brief with sourced facts, open questions and commitment limits.
loop.check: Check factual references, document dates, disclosure permissions and fidelity to the mandate.
loop.stop: One brief and one repair attempt; conflicting sources remain flagged for human resolution.
loop.why_not_simpler: Background correspondence contains varied arguments and context that fixed fields cannot summarise adequately.

steps.what: Meet participants, understand their concerns and represent the authorised position.
Prepare and submit an outcome report to the executive.

loop.input: Assistant's meeting notes, proposed commitments and mandate.
loop.output: Outcome report distinguishing agreed actions, proposals and decisions awaiting authority.
loop.check: Trace statements to notes; verify owners, dates and commitment status with the assistant.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; missing or disputed commitments remain explicitly unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes vary in wording and structure; producing a faithful narrative requires bounded language interpretation.

steps.what: Send agreed follow-up messages and request decisions on commitments outside the mandate.

tasks.design: Link the approved mandate and selected background records in {DOCS} to the meeting in {CALENDAR}. Bounded loops prepare the brief and outcome report, while the assistant conducts the meeting and checks commitments. A configured flow in {WORKFLOW} creates actions in {PROJECT} and queues follow-up messages in {EMAIL} for release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Background information is scattered, and preparing a reliable brief takes reading time. Representation itself depends on trust and contextual judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled document selection and bounded drafting can reduce preparation and reporting effort. Configured action routing removes repeated copying.
tasks.still_hard: Reading the room, protecting relationships and judging what can be promised remain human work. Missing context can make a polished brief misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Earn trust, notice unstated concerns and know when to pause rather than commit the executive.

ambition.what: A scheduled listening session for remote-office employees under an explicit executive mandate.

tasks.altitude: Most meeting time remains human. Less preparation and reporting may make another listening session feasible, but negotiating authority changes only through an explicit mandate.

reach.task: Turn stakeholder concerns into tracked actions and decision requests.
reach.learn: Separate commitments from proposals, assign accountable owners and escalate unresolved dependencies.

evidence.claim: Human representation requires interpersonal judgement; preparation and follow-up can be supported separately.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported drafting and meeting-summary savings, without establishing overall productivity gains.

assumptions: The meeting is already scheduled; this task covers representation, preparation and follow-up.
The assistant uses written notes; recording is unnecessary for the proposed design.
Follow-up release cannot approve commitments outside the mandate; those require a separate executive decision.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates, not measured outcomes.
GDPR and EU AI Act obligations apply; access work includes consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which meetings the assistant may attend as a representative.
Which documents may be used for preparation and disclosed to participants.
How executive mandates and commitment approvals are recorded.
Whether saved preparation time would support additional listening sessions.
research_questions: Does the generated brief omit politically or personally important context?
Can reviewers reliably distinguish proposals from authorised commitments?
Which follow-up messages fit fixed templates?
new_work: Select authorised source material and check brief completeness.
Review reports for commitment status and sensitive wording.
Maintain mandate templates and follow-up routing.
Track decisions awaiting executive authority.
tasks.statement: Meet with individuals, special interest groups, and others on behalf of executives, committees, and boards of directors.

tasks.short: Develop office procedures, secure approval, publish them and oversee their use.

steps.what: Collect existing procedures, service problems and requests for changes.
Assess gaps, responsibilities and practical constraints.
Draft the procedure, responsibilities and exception route.

loop.input: Approved procedure template, current procedure and human-written requirements.
loop.output: Draft procedure with responsibilities, exceptions and marked gaps.
loop.check: Trace requirements to sections; flag invented obligations, missing owners and contradictory instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unresolved contradictions return to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but translating varied requirements into clear instructions needs language generation.

steps.what: Discuss the draft with affected departments and resolve competing needs.
Approve the procedure and its effective date.
Publish the approved version and notify affected employees.
Compile reported exceptions and overdue procedural actions.
Decide which reported problems need correction or management escalation.

tasks.design: Configure a procedure register, change intake and approval flow in {WORKFLOW}, linked to controlled versions in {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts procedures from agreed requirements, while people resolve trade-offs and approve publication. Configured reports replace the exception workbook and feed a regular procedure review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change requests, approvals and exceptions sit in separate documents and mail threads. Local procedure differences make a universal template insufficient.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records and approval features can handle most coordination. Small integrations and bounded drafting make a tailored implementation more affordable.
tasks.still_hard: Agreement on responsibilities, employee impacts and workable exceptions remains organisational work. Poor reporting can hide whether a procedure works.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate a procedure that departments can follow and recognise when an exception exposes a bad rule.

ambition.what: A monthly decision on one recurring office-service bottleneck.

tasks.altitude: The assistant replaces document chasing with testing proposed improvements and reviewing service problems. They can receive delegated authority for small procedural corrections within agreed limits.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a process change improves service.
reach.learn: Map a process, establish a baseline and compare outcomes before recommending wider adoption.

evidence.claim: Procedure registers, version control and approval routing are established deterministic capabilities.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation found drafting time savings but no evidence of higher overall productivity.

assumptions: Time shares describe a procedure-change cycle including oversight; they are planning estimates.
Management retains approval authority for substantive policy changes.
Exception reporting measures service problems rather than individual employee performance.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Any staff monitoring or automated task allocation needs separate assessment.
Consultation effort includes works-council or employee involvement where national rules apply; elapsed consultation may take longer.
unknowns: Who can approve office procedures and delegate minor corrections.
Whether the existing systems support versioned publication and approval records.
Which procedures affect employee rights or working conditions.
Which national consultation rules and agreements apply.
research_questions: Which coordination delays can existing configuration remove?
Can staff follow a revised procedure without informal explanations?
Which service measure would reveal whether the procedure improved?

Review draft instructions for invented requirements.
Check exception-report completeness and access.
Retire obsolete procedures and verify links after publication.
tasks.statement: Set up and oversee administrative policies and procedures for offices or organizations.

tasks.short: Review office procedures, reporting and spending to recommend practical improvements.

steps.what: Agree the process, problem and limits of the review.
Retrieve spending and workflow records for the agreed period.
Reconcile exports and calculate spending, volumes and turnaround times.
Ask staff how work actually flows and where delays arise.
Compare written procedures with observed practice and reporting requirements.

loop.input: Approved procedures, reporting requirements and staff-validated process observations.
loop.output: Draft differences table with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require references for each finding; the assistant verifies meaning, omissions and conflicting evidence.
loop.stop: One comparison and one repair attempt; missing or conflicting evidence goes to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Procedures and observations express equivalent or conflicting requirements in varied prose.

steps.what: Assess improvement options against cost, service quality and staff constraints.
Prepare a recommendation with costs, measures and a proposed trial.
Decide whether to approve a trial and assign responsibility.
Compare trial results with the baseline and report unresolved effects.

tasks.design: Scheduled, read-only connectors on the {DATA_PLATFORM} retrieve scoped records from the {ERP} and {PROJECT}; deterministic checks produce a baseline and trial comparisons in the {BI}. A bounded loop compares procedures in the {DOCS} with validated observations, and a template generator assembles the assistant's selected recommendation. Staff discussions, trade-offs and change approval remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Exports use different identifiers and definitions. Written procedures omit informal workarounds, so a report alone cannot explain delays or establish a good change.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes small connectors, reconciliation checks and report templates cheaper to build. Bounded text comparison can prepare findings with references for review.
tasks.still_hard: Poor records limit causal claims, and lower spending can conceal extra work elsewhere. GDPR, access controls and national employee consultation rules apply; individual monitoring would require separate assessment under the EU AI Act.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish useful controls from avoidable friction and negotiate changes that staff can sustain.

ambition.what: Monthly decisions on whether office workflow trials should continue

tasks.altitude: Less time goes to rebuilding evidence packs, leaving more time to test explanations with staff. With explicit delegation, the assistant could initiate small, reversible trials within agreed service and budget limits.

reach.task: Evaluate whether a process change improved service.
reach.learn: Metric definitions, comparison groups, confounding factors and whole-process costs.

reach.task: Prioritise office improvement spending.
reach.learn: Business cases, service commitments and budget authority.

evidence.claim: Scheduled exports, deterministic reconciliation, dashboards and template reports are established patterns; this digest provides no direct case for this exact task.
A bounded text comparison can prepare procedure findings, but its accuracy and time savings need local testing.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported drafting savings but no evidence of higher productivity and observed hallucinations.
Employment-related monitoring or allocation can bring additional EU AI Act requirements; ordinary report preparation is a different use.

Today, exports from the {ERP} and {PROJECT} are consolidated in the {SPREADSHEET}.
The baseline uses process-level measures rather than individual employee rankings.

Consent and access ranges include consultation work where applicable; elapsed approval time may be longer.

How much time is currently spent collecting evidence versus assessing changes?

Verify source references and challenge unsupported procedure findings.
Maintain connectors, report templates and access permissions.
Check whether trial outcomes reflect the change or other events.
Retire measures and reports that no longer inform decisions.
tasks.statement: Review operating practices and procedures to determine whether improvements can be made in areas such as workflow, reporting procedures, or expenditures.

tasks.short: Explain administrative policies to employees and resolve questions about their application.

steps.what: Receive an employee question and clarify the circumstances.
Locate the current policy and relevant procedure.
Judge how the policy applies and identify questions requiring the policy owner.
Write and send an explanation with the relevant policy references.

loop.input: Clarified question, current policy extracts and the assistant's case interpretation.
loop.output: Short explanation with policy references and unresolved issues.
loop.check: Verify each claim against a current extract; preserve the supplied interpretation and exception limits.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; missing support returns the case to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Varied employee circumstances need tailored wording; fixed replies cover only recurring questions.

steps.what: Discuss sensitive implications or remaining misunderstandings with the employee.
Record the outcome and forward unresolved exceptions to the policy owner.

tasks.design: A question register in {WORKFLOW} links employee questions to current, permission-controlled policies in {DOCS}. Deterministic lookup retrieves approved extracts, and a bounded drafting loop prepares explanations for review before release through {EMAIL}. The assistant handles sensitive discussions and refers exceptions to the policy owner.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies have inconsistent titles, versions and ownership. Finding an authoritative answer often requires personal knowledge.
tasks.enabler_now: A small policy index and configured intake can remove repeated searching. Bounded drafting can turn an approved interpretation into readable advice.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting policies and unusual circumstances require a responsible policy owner. Better wording cannot resolve missing authority.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a technically correct answer would mislead or distress someone, and explain its practical consequences.

ambition.what: A monthly policy-friction brief showing recurring ambiguities for policy owners.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time finding documents and more time resolving sensitive questions. They can propose policy clarifications; exception approval remains with the policy owner.

reach.task: Prioritise improvements to office procedures.
reach.learn: Group recurring questions by cause and describe a change with measurable service effects.

evidence.claim: Policy retrieval and exception routing can use indexed records and deterministic rules; interpretation still needs judgement.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation observed hallucinations, supporting source checks before releasing drafted advice.

assumptions: This describes a typical mid-size European office; shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
The policy register identifies current versions, access rights and responsible owners.
Lookup uses policy categories and metadata; ambiguous searches return to a person.
GDPR applies to employee questions. EU AI Act literacy requirements apply to relevant AI use.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; statutory waiting periods may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether policies have reliable version status and named owners.
Which questions the assistant may answer without policy-owner involvement.
How many requests concern sensitive personal circumstances.
Which national consultation requirements apply.

How often do reviewers materially change a drafted explanation?

Review drafted explanations and unsupported claims.
Inspect unresolved referrals and recurring policy gaps.
Maintain access rules and question-record retention.
tasks.statement: Interpret administrative and operating policies and procedures for employees.

tasks.short: Answer calls, identify the right recipient, connect callers or record messages.

steps.what: Greet the caller and establish their identity and purpose.
Check the contact directory and recipient availability.
Choose whether to connect, take a message or escalate.
Transfer an accepted call to the selected recipient.
Record a message and send it to the responsible recipient.

tasks.design: Configure a permission-filtered contact directory and availability view beside the {TELEPHONY}, using {DOCS} and {CALENDAR}. The assistant chooses the disposition; the {TELEPHONY} executes that approved transfer, while a structured message form in {WORKFLOW} sends callback details through {EMAIL} or {CHAT}. No recording or language model is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contact ownership and availability were scattered, and message formats differed. Much of this was already technically possible but poorly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing directory, presence and message-form features can cover most supporting work. AI-assisted coding can shorten development of any missing connector.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising a sensitive caller, handling distress and protecting an executive's availability remain situational decisions.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant reads tone, preserves relationships and decides when an interruption is justified.
tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer directory searches and repeated message entries. Call-screening authority stays within the existing delegation; no new decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Maintain the shared contact directory and callback queue.
reach.learn: Service ownership, availability permissions and escalation paths.

evidence.claim: Directory lookup, structured messages and approved call transfers generally need configuration rather than a model.
The digest provides no documented executive call-handling case supporting a quantified saving.

assumptions: Step shares are estimates across connected calls and message-taking calls, not a single mandatory sequence.
The assistant may read approved availability status without seeing private appointment details.
Build ranges estimate working effort for one team, including access review and applicable employee consultation under national rules.
A personal setup starts with the assistant's authorised contacts; shared routing requires team access.
unknowns: Whether the {TELEPHONY} supports directory lookup and controlled transfers.
Which recipients permit availability sharing and which callers have special access.
Call volumes, message-taking frequency and current handling time.
Applicable consultation requirements under national rules.

Does a trial reduce handling time without increasing misroutes or revealing private availability?
new_work: Update contact ownership and escalation paths.
Resolve failed transfers and undelivered messages.
Review access permissions when roles change.
tasks.statement: Answer phone calls and direct calls to appropriate parties or take messages.

tasks.short: Order office supplies, maintain office records and prepare basic bookkeeping entries.

steps.what: Collect supply requests and check available office stock.
Select approved items and create a purchase requisition.
Approve the purchase requisition against budget and purchasing policy.
Issue the purchase order to the approved supplier.
Check delivered supplies against the order and record shortages or damage.
Update office records and supporting documents when changes arrive.
Enter supplier invoice details, select coding and check purchase evidence.
Review exceptions and approve the accounting entry for posting.

tasks.design: Configure request forms, approved catalogues and purchase approvals in {PROCUREMENT}, with receipt capture and invoice matching in {ERP}. Maintain office records through validated forms in {DOCS}; use a small deterministic integration through {WORKFLOW} only where existing connections are missing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Small requests arrive informally, receipt evidence is incomplete, and purchasing and finance records are maintained separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Catalogue ordering, invoice capture, matching and approval rules are established features. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of connecting them and replacing repeated entry.
tasks.still_hard: Physical stock checks, disputed deliveries, unusual accounting treatment and incomplete invoices remain. Savings depend on features already available in the installed systems.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant spots practical supply problems and knows when an apparently routine purchase needs finance or management attention.

ambition.what: A weekly review of office replenishment needs against expected demand.

tasks.altitude: Routine entry becomes exception review and physical verification. The assistant can adjust replenishment quantities within approved limits; budget approval and accounting policy remain with their current owners.

reach.task: Plan office supply levels and supplier service.
reach.learn: Reorder levels, demand patterns, purchasing controls and invoice matching.

evidence.claim: Catalogue requisitions, approval thresholds and invoice matching are established business-system capabilities.
Structured record updates and accounting templates usually require validation rules rather than generative models.

assumptions: The steps represent three recurring workstreams; office record maintenance is independent of purchasing.
Approved catalogues, cost centres and purchasing permissions exist.
Existing invoice capture can propose fields; unsupported documents enter an exception queue.
No bank payments or supplier bank-detail changes are included.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
GDPR applies to personal information in office and invoice records.
unknowns: Which purchasing and invoice features are licensed and configured?
How often are invoices unmatched, handwritten or outside standard tax treatment?
Which office records are maintained, and who authorises their changes?
What access separation and employee consultation are required under local policy and national rules?

Which receipt and invoice exceptions account for most handling time?

Resolve missing receipts, invoice mismatches and unusual record changes.
Review captured invoice fields and proposed accounting entries.
Monitor failed transfers and duplicate-order controls.
tasks.statement: Perform general office duties, such as ordering supplies, maintaining records management database systems, and performing basic bookkeeping work.

tasks.short: Prepare meeting agendas, coordinate rooms and catering, and distribute meeting papers.

steps.what: Collect agenda proposals, attendance requirements and meeting deadlines.
Draft the agenda from proposals, previous actions and the chair's priorities.

loop.input: Agenda proposals, previous actions, meeting template and recorded chair priorities.
loop.output: Draft agenda with proposed timings and source references.
loop.check: Check every item against a proposal or previous action; validate total meeting duration.
loop.stop: One draft and one validation pass per meeting; unresolved items return to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates handle layout, but proposals need concise wording and consolidation.

steps.what: Agree agenda priorities and sensitive items with the chair.
Reserve a suitable room and required meeting equipment.
Request catering options and check costs against meeting requirements.
Approve catering expenditure or request changes.
Confirm catering quantities, delivery details and approved price with the supplier.
Send the approved agenda and current meeting papers to authorised attendees.
Check room readiness and resolve last-minute participant needs.

tasks.design: Configure a meeting request and checklist in {WORKFLOW}, room rules in {CALENDAR}, and approved supplier options in {PROCUREMENT}. A bounded drafting step prepares the agenda in {DOCS}; the chair approves priorities, the budget holder approves spending, and {EMAIL} sends approved orders and reviewed meeting packs.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrive in separate messages, supplier details vary, and the chair's priorities are rarely recorded consistently.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing booking and approval features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of connecting records and templates; a small model loop can consolidate agenda prose.
tasks.still_hard: Political priorities, late changes, accessibility needs and unusual supplier requests still require personal coordination.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices tensions, protects the chair's attention and makes participants feel expected.

ambition.what: A pre-meeting readiness review for committee chairs.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time chasing inputs and more time resolving readiness risks with chairs. They can resolve routine logistics within an agreed budget; agenda priorities remain with the chair.

reach.task: Plan room capacity and event support.
reach.learn: Room constraints, accessibility requirements and supplier service standards.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can create an agenda and meeting invitation from an email thread.
The UK departmental evaluation found scheduling took longer on average; local testing must establish any gain.
Booking rules, approval routing and structured supplier orders are established configuration patterns.

Dates are already agreed, rooms have shared booking records, and routine catering has approved options.
Supplier confirmations can be sent automatically only within the approved proposal.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.

Who may approve spending and release confidential meeting papers?
