Maintain room constraints, supplier options and spending limits.
Handle missing inputs, booking conflicts and supplier failures.
Check that released packs contain the approved document versions.
tasks.statement: Prepare agendas and make arrangements, such as coordinating catering for luncheons, for committee, board, and other meetings.

tasks.short: Coordinate office records, departmental spending, budgets, personnel referrals and workplace services.

steps.what: Collect office service requests and status updates from the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Authorised office service correspondence, excluding restricted personnel case contents.
loop.output: Draft category, requested outcome, deadline and source reference.
loop.check: Validate required fields and source access; keep sensitive contents outside the shared register.
loop.stop: One extraction; uncertain or sensitive requests enter a restricted assistant queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests arrive in varied free text; structured service forms bypass extraction.

steps.what: Judge urgency, confidentiality and the responsible service team.
Update departmental records and document permissions in the {DOCS}.
Combine {ERP} spending extracts and commitments in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Prepare budget scenarios and service-cost estimates in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Agree spending limits, service priorities and unresolved resource trade-offs.
Coordinate confidential personnel referrals through restricted {EMAIL} correspondence.
Raise housekeeping and workplace service requests in the {HELPDESK}.
Inspect service completion and resolve recurring supplier or staff concerns.

tasks.design: Configure a service register and routing in the {WORKFLOW}, connected to the {HELPDESK}, with a bounded extractor for incoming {EMAIL} requests. Deterministic jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile {ERP} spending and commitments, generate budget scenarios and feed a {BI} backlog view; configured filing handles approved records in the {DOCS}. Personnel cases stay in restricted channels, while people decide priorities, budgets and service acceptance.
tasks.previous_blocker: Office coordination crossed departmental boundaries without shared request records, consistent cost mappings or clear service ownership.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, queues and permissions can be configured; small integrations can connect spending, commitments and service status.
tasks.still_hard: Service trade-offs, personnel confidentiality, supplier disputes and national consultation requirements remain contextual.
tasks.human_edge: Getting teams to accept practical compromises while protecting sensitive personnel information.

ambition.what: A weekly office service capacity and backlog review for department heads.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends more time resolving recurring service failures and presenting costed choices. With delegation, they can reprioritise service requests within approved budgets and escalate capacity shortages earlier.

reach.task: Plan office service capacity and address recurring backlog causes.
reach.learn: Service levels, demand patterns, capacity planning and delegated spending.

reach.task: Evaluate housekeeping service quality and supplier performance.
reach.learn: Acceptance criteria, service inspections and contract escalation.

evidence.claim: Configured queues, approval routes and deterministic reconciliation can reduce coordination paperwork.
The EU AI Act has specific provisions for AI used in staff task allocation or monitoring; intake extraction needs a narrower assessment.
Dutch works-council rules cited in the digest cover certain staff-data and monitoring arrangements; national rules elsewhere vary.

assumptions: Shares describe a mixed service portfolio; each request follows the relevant branch.
A {HELPDESK} handles workplace requests, while a {SPREADSHEET} ties spending and commitments together.
Personnel decisions remain with authorised managers and the human resources team.
The shared register contains service metadata rather than personnel case contents.
Build ranges cover an initial departmental scope and consultation effort; elapsed consultation may take longer.
unknowns: Which office services and budgets fall within the assistant's authority?
Are service responsibilities and acceptance criteria documented?
Can commitments and actual spending be matched by department and service?
Which personnel information may the assistant access under GDPR and internal access rules?
Which national employee-consultation rules apply to service records and dashboards?
research_questions: Which recurring service failures arise from unclear ownership rather than insufficient capacity?
Can budget scenarios be generated from explicit assumptions without narrative interpretation?
Which backlog measures support service planning without becoming individual staff monitoring?
new_work: Review ambiguous or sensitive intake drafts.
Maintain service categories, team routing and escalation thresholds.
Resolve unmatched commitments and stale service statuses.
Review register permissions, record retention and dashboard scope.
Update budget assumptions and service acceptance criteria.
tasks.statement: Coordinate and direct office services, such as records, departmental finances, budget preparation, personnel issues, and housekeeping, to aid executives.

tasks.short: Handle administrative requests for other departments, including documents, record updates and routine correspondence.

steps.what: Read departmental requests and identify the requested administrative output.

loop.input: A support request and an approved catalogue of request types.
loop.output: A draft request record containing output type, requester, deadline and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate against the catalogue and required fields; retain the source request beside extracted values.
loop.stop: One extraction attempt; ambiguous or unsupported requests enter the clarification queue.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing requests arrive as varied free text. A configured form handles new structured submissions.

steps.what: Clarify scope, urgency and missing information with the requesting department.
Find current records, approved templates and supporting information.
Prepare the requested document or routine correspondence from approved information.
Check departmental facts and approve the output.
Return the approved output and confirm completion.

tasks.design: Configure a request register in the {WORKFLOW}, with structured forms and bounded extraction for requests arriving through the {EMAIL}. Deterministic lookups assemble permitted records from the {DOCS}, and template generators prepare standard outputs for departmental approval before delivery.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests mixed missing information, informal priorities and many document variants. A shared mailbox provided flexibility but little reusable structure.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, approval flows and template generation already cover much of the work. Small integrations and bounded request extraction make the remaining gaps cheaper to address.
tasks.still_hard: Unusual requests need negotiation and bespoke work. Departmental record quality and template ownership limit reuse.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant understands what colleagues actually need, negotiates realistic deadlines and handles requests that do not fit a standard service.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on which cross-department request bottleneck to remove.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving incomplete requests and improving recurring administrative services. With delegation, the assistant can sequence standard requests within agreed service levels; departmental content approval stays with the department.

reach.task: Triage a shared request backlog and identify blocked dependencies.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, dependency mapping and practical service-level measures.

evidence.claim: Forms, record lookups, templates and approval flows suit repeatable clerical requests without autonomous agents.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation reported drafting time savings, but these do not establish gains for this mixed clerical workload.
Step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates for a limited request catalogue.

assumptions: The steps represent common document and correspondence requests; specialist transactions require their own departmental workflow.
The pilot starts with a few recurring request types and approved templates.
Outputs are delivered internally; external commitments require the relevant delegated authority.
GDPR applies to personal information in requests and source records.
Build ranges cover working effort; national consultation and access decisions may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: The most frequent request types and their actual time distribution.
Which departments maintain authoritative records and current templates.
The assistant's authority to prioritise requests or update departmental records.
Whether proposed queue reporting would monitor individual employees and trigger national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which request types can use structured forms and templates without losing necessary flexibility?
Does clarification effort fall after introducing required fields?
If staff allocation or monitoring is added, does the intended use fall within EU AI Act Annex III?
new_work: Resolve ambiguous requests and unsupported request types.
Maintain forms, templates, lookup mappings and service definitions.
Check that source access remains limited to the requesting department's needs.
Review bottlenecks without turning service reporting into unnecessary employee monitoring.
tasks.statement: Provide clerical support to other departments.

tasks.short: Collect, validate and submit approved employee changes and time information for payroll processing.

steps.what: Retrieve approved employee changes, absence records and time information.
Request missing submissions and approvals before the payroll cutoff.
Resolve disputed or incomplete submissions with the responsible manager.
Combine approved inputs into the monthly payroll worksheet.
Enter or upload payroll inputs into the payroll system.
Reconcile input totals and investigate validation errors or unexpected changes.
Approve the reconciled payroll input batch for processing.

tasks.design: Configure cutoff reminders and approved input exports from the {HCM}, then map those records directly into a staged batch in the {PAYROLL}. Deterministic checks reconcile identifiers, effective dates, duplicates and control totals; the assistant resolves exceptions and the payroll lead approves processing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different identifiers, effective-date rules and approval formats made copying into a worksheet convenient. Reliable integration also required access and agreement on authoritative records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing export and import functions support structured transfer. Small deterministic mappings and reconciliation checks can be built and maintained with less coding effort.
tasks.still_hard: Retroactive changes, disputed hours and national payroll rules require payroll expertise. An interface must distinguish staging from processing and prevent duplicate submissions.
tasks.human_edge: People resolve disputed entitlements, understand unusual employment circumstances and take responsibility for payroll approval.

ambition.what: A weekly decision on unresolved payroll-input exceptions before cutoff.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time consolidating and retyping data and more time resolving missing approvals before cutoff. Payroll calculation, entitlement interpretation and payment authority remain with authorised payroll and finance roles; no new formal rights are assumed.

reach.task: Coordinate payroll-input readiness across departments.
reach.learn: Payroll cutoffs, effective dates, reconciliation controls and separation of duties.

evidence.claim: Structured payroll inputs suit configured exports, deterministic mappings and reconciliation rather than model interpretation.
Staging, duplicate prevention, control totals and approval separation are established integration controls.
The digest provides no documented payroll implementation or measured payroll saving; effort and build ranges are estimates.

assumptions: The assistant prepares payroll inputs rather than calculating pay, filing returns or releasing bank payments.
A worksheet commonly bridges approved records and payroll import in this representative workflow.
Only approved changes are transferred; entitlement decisions are not inferred from free text.
The target interface supports staging without triggering a pay run.
The pilot covers one payroll population and includes parallel reconciliation across payroll cycles.
GDPR requires restricted access and data minimisation; national employment and consultation rules vary.
Build ranges describe working effort; payroll-cycle timing and consultation may extend elapsed rollout.
unknowns: Whether the existing systems already provide a supported connection that only needs configuration.
The actual source of time records and the assistant's permitted payroll access.
Employee identifier mappings, pay codes and retroactive-change rules.
Whether uploads stage inputs or immediately affect processing.
Existing approval roles, payroll calendars and national requirements.
Whether employee or works-council consultation is required for the proposed change.
research_questions: Can native integration eliminate the worksheet without custom code?
Can imports be retried without creating duplicate payroll changes?
Which reconciliation checks detect materially wrong inputs before approval?
new_work: Investigate failed mappings, missing approvals and unexpected variances.
Maintain pay-code mappings, cutoff calendars and effective-date rules.
Reconcile transferred records after interface or payroll configuration changes.
Review access logs and remove unnecessary payroll-data copies.
Retest duplicate prevention and staging behaviour after system updates.
tasks.statement: Process payroll information.

tasks.short: Supervise clerical staff, coach individuals and arrange training.

steps.what: Review upcoming work and training records to identify coverage gaps.
Discuss difficulties, learning needs and development interests with clerical staff.
Assign routine work and approve training within delegated limits.
Adapt procedures and examples into training materials.

loop.input: Approved procedures, learning objectives and selected examples without unnecessary personal data.
loop.output: Training draft with exercises and references to source sections.
loop.check: Check source references, procedural accuracy and suitability for the learner before release.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair attempt; unresolved sections return to manual editing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates provide structure, but adapting prose and examples to learning needs requires language interpretation.

steps.what: Enrol staff in agreed courses.
Find suitable times and send training invitations.
Demonstrate tasks, observe practice and give individual feedback.
Record attendance and verified course completion.
Review progress with staff and agree further support.

tasks.design: Configure the {LMS} and {CALENDAR} to enrol staff, schedule agreed training and record verified completion. A small service on the {DATA_PLATFORM} combines training records with the {PROJECT} work plan to flag factual coverage gaps, while a bounded drafting loop prepares materials from approved procedures in the {DOCS}. The assistant approves materials and handles coaching, work allocation and individual support.
tasks.previous_blocker: Training records, work plans and procedures sit separately. Individual coaching needs cannot be reduced to course completion rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing enrolment and calendar settings handle routine administration. AI coding reduces the effort of building connectors and templates; bounded drafting can adapt approved material.
tasks.still_hard: Completion does not prove competence. GDPR limits access and reuse of staff information; national rules may require consultation, and automated staff allocation or monitoring would need a separate EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Notice hesitation, build trust, demonstrate judgement and adapt feedback to the person.

ambition.what: Cross-cover training for part-time clerical staff

tasks.altitude: The week contains more coaching and practical cross-cover exercises. With manager delegation, the assistant could approve routine cross-training within an agreed budget; the software itself grants no decision rights.

reach.task: Plan clerical service coverage during absence.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, service priorities and the limits of delegated staffing authority.

reach.task: Coordinate training for a procedure rollout.
reach.learn: Dependencies, adoption measures and rollout planning.

evidence.claim: Enrolment rules, calendar configuration and record connectors are established implementation patterns; local savings are estimates.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can prepare an invitation and agenda from a mail thread; this supports scheduling preparation, not supervision.
The Department for Business and Trade evaluation found scheduling took longer, supporting a configuration-first approach and local testing.
The EU AI Act includes AI literacy obligations and provisions concerning employment-related allocation and monitoring.

assumptions: The assistant has delegated responsibility for routine clerical work allocation and training coordination.
A typical setup uses the {LMS}, {PROJECT}, {CALENDAR} and {DOCS}; local arrangements vary.
Time shares and remaining percentages are planning estimates, informed by the supplied priors.
Automatic enrolment and invitations stay within an approved training plan and spending limits.
Build ranges cover a small pilot using existing systems, not a replacement learning platform.
unknowns: Which systems hold training records, work plans and approved procedures?
Can the installed {LMS} configure enrolments, completion evidence and calendar connections?
Which training and work-allocation decisions are delegated to the assistant?
Which national consultation requirements and employee representative arrangements apply?
Are approved materials current, accessible and suitable for reuse?
What is the measured local time split?
research_questions: Does configuration cover enrolment and scheduling without a custom connector?
Can factual coverage gaps be shown without scoring individual performance?
Do adapted exercises improve observed task competence after review?
new_work: Review generated training materials and their source references.
Handle unavailable courses, scheduling conflicts and missing completion evidence.
Maintain course mappings, access permissions and connectors.
Refresh training examples when approved procedures change.
tasks.statement: Supervise and train other clerical staff and arrange for employee training by scheduling training or organizing training material.

Management analyst: prepare reconciled spending explanations and recurring variance reviews.
Administrative services manager: plan service capacity and address recurring operational failures.
Facilities manager: assess service quality and supplier follow-through.

Administrative services manager: measure correspondence handoffs and improve escalation arrangements.

Configure approvals, permissions and document metadata.
Measure handling time, review effort and rework.

Project management specialist: track administrative dependencies and meeting actions.

Request design, template maintenance and workflow configuration.
Permission management, GDPR basics and appropriate AI use.
Reconciliation, exception analysis and effective-date handling.

role_batches.altitude: The week shifts from searching, rewriting and chasing records toward resolving ambiguity, preparing executives and tracking decisions. New decision rights are limited to explicitly delegated procedural corrections and meeting mandates.

Procedure mapping and service measurement.

reach: Administrative services management through service coverage and training planning.
Management analysis through baseline measures and evaluation of process trials.
Project coordination through procedure rollouts and adoption support.

Process mapping and metric definition.

Checking generated text against approved sources.
